newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI repo auctions seen propping call rates.
newsitem.headline: India RBI repo auctions seen propping call rates.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) which revived repos auctions this month, may use it as a regular tool to prevent call rates from falling too low, treasury managers and dealers said on Wednesday.
"As long as there is excess liquidity, the RBI will issue repos," Subrata Das, director at Mata Securities, said.
He said the RBI will stop the auctions as soon as call rates cross the 5.0 percent mark.
Call rates have been below the 5.0 percent mark in January.

"It's a way of signalling bankers the RBI would intervene if the call rates fell too low," he said. Das wanted the RBI to issue 14-day repos auctions which would help the central bank raise 25 to 30 billion rupees at 6.0 percent level.
RBI conducted regular repos auctions of three to four days duration in January and on Tuesday announced a similar schedule for February.
Repos auctions used to be a regular affair in 1994-95 but was discontinued later, dealers said.
Besides keeping call rates at stable levels, repos auctions can also keep a check on broad money supply growth which impacts inflation, M. Srinivas, senior manager at Centurion Bank said.
The extent of excess liquidity in the system can be gauged from the amounts raised by the RBI through these auctions, R. Narayan, assistant manager (treasury) at Bank of Nova Scotia in Bombay said.
M. Venkatramani, chief money market dealer at Banque Nationale De Paris said the RBI may not have to resort to repos auctions in March.
"Bankers expect credit to pick up by March -- banks will also try and park the funds in the most short-dated and treasury bills on which the return more than the repo acution interest," he said.
